_comment: The quantities recorded every morning and every evening, in the order they
appear in the table. Editing this file is how a quantity is added, renamed or
given its PV -- no code change is needed.
A row is:
key      unique, never changes; it is the column name in spfe_log.csv
label    what stands in the second column of the table
pvs      one PV name per number in the cell. Empty string = not filled in yet;
the cell then shows a dash. A row with no pvs at all is manual.
join     what separates the numbers of a multi-PV row (default ';')
unit     shown in the Quantity column, in brackets, after the label. It is
never typed into a value cell -- only the number is typed.
decimals how many decimal places
round    the step each number is shown to: 10 = to the nearest ten, 100 = to
the nearest hundred, 1 = whole numbers. One entry per PV, or a single
number for the whole row. Only the SCREEN and the workbook are
rounded -- spfe_log.csv keeps the measured value, so the
out-of-range statistics still see the real spread.
manual   'text' or 'number' -- typed by the operator instead of read from a PV
default  what a manual row shows until somebody types over it. Written into
the record when a moment is recorded, so the file says what the
screen says. Typing over it changes that one day only.
default_from  the first day the default counts. Days before it show an empty
cell that can still be typed into, and nothing is written into the
files -- a setting cannot be claimed for a day that predates it.
url      makes the label a link; clicking it opens the address in a browser
check    false switches the out-of-range statistics off for this row
STILL TO BE FILLED IN: Pumplaser DAC, Humidity, Oscillator Power, Oscillator
Bandwidth and DAZZ2 have no PV -- the archiver has no channel with pump, dac,
humid, osc or dazz in its name. L3-SPFE-AOD03-002 is the only dazzler the
archiver knows; DAZZ1 reads its Power_RB.
A dazzler has ONE percentage, not two. The second number the table used to
show (Amplitude_RB, labelled 'intensity') was a guess and is gone.
